about.title: Martinez Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Contra Costa County recorded 2 traffic deaths in Martinez in the most recent final crash year, alongside 116 injury collisions on roads like Alhambra Avenue, SR-4, and I-680. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to figure out what comes next. California wrongful death law gives certain surviving family members — starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children — the right to pursue a civil claim separate from any criminal case tied to the crash. That claim can address funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance. There's a two-year window from the date of death to file, and it's shorter if a government entity is involved, which matters on roads maintained by the city or Caltrans. Our team handles wrongful death claims in Martinez and can walk through your options at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Martinez Choose Us

items.title: Standing Can Be Limited
items.desc: California law restricts who may bring a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then certain other dependents or heirs. We can help sort out who in your family qualifies to file.

items.title: The Filing Window Moves Fast
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that window shrinks considerably if a government entity — like the city or Caltrans, which maintain roads such as SR-4 — is involved. Waiting to sort out details can cost your family the chance to file at all.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: A wrongful death claim can account for lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance your family relied on, not just burial expenses. We can help make sure those less obvious losses aren't left out.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Martinez?
items.answer: Generally, California gives surviving family members two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. That deadline is shorter if a government entity, such as the city of Martinez or Caltrans, had a role in the roadway or crash. We can confirm the exact deadline that applies to your situation.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California limits standing mostly to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children first. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. This is one of the first things we will help clarify.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to any criminal charges filed after a Martinez crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case tied to the same collision. Even if criminal charges are filed, delayed, or never pursued, your family may still have the right to bring a civil claim. The two processes run independently of each other.
